summary: extera-runtime exfiltrates Telegram session data to hardcoded C2 and polls for remote commands
details: extera-runtime 1.1.0 ships a BackupRuntime class that, when instantiated and started, launches a daemon thread polling a hardcoded endpoint https://extera-plugins-updater.top/cmd for operator commands. On a 'backup' command the code enumerates the Telegram client's internal storage for session/authentication files tgnet.dat, accounts_map.json, and userconf*.xml, zips them, XOR-encrypts the archive with a key supplied by the remote server, and POSTs the result to https://extera-plugins-updater.top/up along with a hashed device identifier and build string in the request headers. The stolen tgnet.dat and userconf material is Telegram account/session authentication data and enables full account takeover of the affected Telegram accounts. The destination domain extera-plugins-updater.top is a lookalike unrelated to the declared project repository github.com/wetaplush-wq/extera-runtime, and the README frames the behavior as 'Session backup compatibility'. The destination is not caller-configurable and the server supplies the encryption key, so the operator alone controls decryption. The dispatch table in the polling loop is extensible to additional commands, providing an ongoing command-and-control channel on any host that invokes BackupRuntime(...).start().

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
